questions.stem: The individual partner rather than the partnership makes which of the following elections?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nonrecognition treatment for involuntary conversion gains.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Code section 179 deductions for tangible personal property.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether to take a deduction or credit for taxes paid to foreign countries.

questions.explanation:
In a partnership (P/S), only a few tax elections are made by the individual partners. Common elections include the treatment of foreign taxes (credit or deduction).

Because a P/S is a flow-through entity (reported on partners' individual tax returns), its activities are divided between ordinary business income or loss and separately stated items. Separately stated items are not part of ordinary business income or loss because these items are subject to statutory tax limitations or special rules when reported on the partners' individual tax returns. The Code requires tax elections affecting the calculation of the P/S ordinary business or loss generally to be made at the P/S level, not by individual partners.

Common elections made by the P/S include the amortization of organizational costs, nonrecognition treatment for involuntary conversion gains, and cost recovery (depreciation) method. Special elections related to depreciation (Section 179 immediate expensing) are still made at the P/S level but are allocated to individual partners as a separately reported item
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップはパススルー事業体であり、通常の事業所得の計算に影響する税務上の選択は原則としてパートナーシップ段階で行う。組織費の償却、非自発的転換による利得の不認識、減価償却方法などはパートナーシップが選択する。Section 179の即時償却もパートナーシップ段階で選択し、個別記載項目としてパートナーに配分される。外国税額を税額控除とするか所得控除とするかは、個々のパートナーが選択する数少ない項目である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.1

questions.stem: The method used to depreciate partnership property is an election made by

choices.label: A
choices.text: The partnership and must be the same method used by the "principal partner."

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partnership and may be any method approved by the IRS.

questions.explanation:
Common elections made by the P/S include selecting the tax year, inventory valuation method, and cost recovery (depreciation) method.

P/S may elect to use any method of depreciation that is approved by the IRS in calculating the P/S ordinary business or loss.
questions.explanationJa: 減価償却方法は、課税年度や棚卸資産の評価方法と同じく、パートナーシップ段階で選択する項目である。パートナーシップは、通常の事業所得の計算にあたりIRSが認める減価償却方法であればどれでも選択できる。主たるパートナーの方法に合わせる必要はなく、各パートナーが個別に選ぶものでもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.2

questions.stem: Day's adjusted basis in LMN Partnership interest is $50,000. During the year, Day received a nonliquidating distribution of $25,000 cash plus land with an adjusted basis of $15,000 to LMN, and a fair market value of $20,000. How much is Day's basis in the land?
questions.explanation:
Nonliquidating partnership distributions generally are nontaxable returns of capital to partners (ie, refunds of partners' investments). However, if cash distributions exceed a partner's basis in the partnership, the amount above basis is a taxable capital gain. Property distributions exceeding basis (after cash distributions), in contrast, are nontaxable when the distributions are made.

Partnership distributions reduce a partner's basis (but not below zero) in the following order:

Cash: Gain is recognized only if cash distributions exceed the partner's basis.

Property: The partnership's basis generally becomes the partner's basis in the property. This is known as carryover basis; it is limited to the partner's remaining basis in the partnership after accounting for cash distributions.

In this scenario, the cash distribution reduces Day's basis in LMN Partnership to $25,000 ($50,000 beginning basis − $25,000 cash). Day's basis in LMN is further reduced by the distributed land's basis. Because the land's carryover basis ($15,000) does not exceed Day's remaining basis ($25,000), Day assumes LMN's $15,000 carried-over basis in the land.
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配は原則として出資の払戻しであり課税されず、分配はパートナーのベーシスを現金、その他の資産の順に減らす。まず現金$25,000でベーシスは$50,000−$25,000＝$25,000になる。土地にはパートナーシップの帳簿価額$15,000が引き継がれ、残りのベーシス$25,000を超えないので、土地のベーシスは$15,000である。時価$20,000は使わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.3

questions.stem: Under Section 444 of the Internal Revenue Code, certain partnerships can elect to use a tax year different from their required tax year. One of the conditions for eligibility to make a Section 444 election is that the partnership must

choices.label: B
choices.text: Be a member of a tiered structure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have a deferral period no longer than 3 months.

questions.explanation:
IRS rules generally require a partnership to adopt the same tax year as that of the partners (or a majority of partnership interests). If the partners are all individuals who report income using calendar year, for example, the partnership itself should adopt a December 31 year end.

A partnership may elect to have a tax year other than what is generally required in either of these two situations:

The partnership makes a Section 444 election

It is not required to cite a valid business reason for the election.

Deferral must not exceed 3 months.

The partnership's business purpose warrants having an alternative year end:

The partnership must provide a valid business reason for ending its tax year at a different time (ski resort's season ends in May).

Deferral may exceed 3 months.
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップは原則として、過半の持分を持つパートナーと同じ課税年度を採用しなければならない。Section 444の選択をすれば、事業上の理由を示さずに別の年度を選べるが、繰延期間は3か月以内でなければならない。正当な事業目的（スキー場のシーズン終了月など）を示す場合は、繰延期間が3か月を超えてもよい。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.4

questions.stem:
A partner's adjusted basis in Lux Partnership was $18,000. The partner received the following nonliquidating partnership distributions:

Cash | $10,000
Substantially appreciated inventory:
Adjusted basis | 4,000
Fair market value | 12,000
Land:
Adjusted basis | 14,000
Fair market value | 20,000

What is the partner's tax basis in the land received from the partnership?
questions.explanation:
Nonliquidating partnership distributions reduce a partner's basis (but not below $0) in the following order:

Cash: This is applied first because a capital gain must be recognized if the cash distribution exceeds the partner's basis in the partnership.

Hot assets: These assets (appreciated inventory) are applied before other property because ordinary income is recognized when a hot asset is sold.

Other property: Generally, the partnership's basis becomes the partner's basis in the property (carryover basis), but it is limited to the partner's remaining basis in the partnership after distributions of cash and hot assets.

In this scenario, the partner's basis in Lux Partnership is reduced first by the cash distribution and then by hot assets (inventory). The partner's basis is further reduced by a portion of the land's adjusted carryover basis ($14,000), limited to the partner's $4,000 remaining basis in Lux. Therefore, the partner's basis in the land is $4,000.

Step: Calculation / Remaining basis
1: $18,000 partner basis in Lux − $10,000 distributed cash / = $8,000
2: $8,000 remaining basis − $4,000 inventory carryover basis / = $4,000
3: $4,000 remaining basis − $4,000 land basis (limited by basis) / = $0
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配はベーシスを、現金、ホットアセット（含み益のある棚卸資産など）、その他の資産の順に減らし、ベーシスは0未満にならない。現金で$18,000−$10,000＝$8,000、棚卸資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額$4,000で$8,000−$4,000＝$4,000が残る。土地の帳簿価額$14,000は残りのベーシス$4,000に制限されるため、土地のベーシスは$4,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.5

questions.stem: Cobb, Danver, and Evans each owned a one-third interest in the capital and profits of their calendar-year partnership. On September 18 of Year 1, Cobb and Danver sold their partnership interests to Frank and immediately withdrew from all participation in the partnership. On March 15 of Year 2, Cobb and Danver received full payment from Frank for the sale of their partnership interests. For tax purposes, the partnership
questions.explanation:
A partnership generally terminates for tax purposes when no part of the business, financial operations, or venture of the partnership is carried on by any of its partners. Here, the partnership did not terminate because there was no agreement to dissolve, wind up the business, and distribute property to the partners. The partnership business continued with original partner Evans (33.33%) and new partner Frank (66.67%).

The Tax Act of 2017 repealed the rule that a partnership be terminated for tax purposes when 50% or more of the partnership interests changed hands within a 12-month period.
questions.explanationJa: 税務上パートナーシップが終了するのは、パートナーの誰によっても事業が一切営まれなくなったときである。本問では解散・清算・財産分配の合意はなく、元のパートナーEvans（3分の1）と新パートナーFrank（3分の2）で事業が続いているため、終了していない。12か月以内に50%以上の持分が移転すると終了するという旧ルールは、2017年税制改正で廃止された。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.6

questions.stem: Gulde's tax basis in Chyme Partnership was $26,000 at the time Gulde received a liquidating distribution of $12,000 cash and land with an adjusted basis to Chyme of $10,000 and a fair market value of $30,000. Chyme did not have unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory, or properties that had been contributed by its partners. What was the amount of Gulde's basis in the land?
questions.explanation:
In general, a liquidating distribution is a nontaxable return of a partner's capital. Liquidating distributions reduce a partner's basis in the partnership to $0 by allocating the partner's basis in the partnership to the distributed assets. The basis in distributed property increases or decreases accordingly to absorb the partner's remaining basis in the partnership.

The basis in a partnership is reduced first by cash and then by hot assets before allocating any remaining basis to other property. In this scenario, the sequence for reducing the basis is as follows:

Remaining basis in Chyme:
Step 1: $26,000 Gulde's basis in Chyme Partnership − $12,000 cash / = / $14,000
Step 2: $14,000 remaining basis − $0 hot assets / = / 14,000
Step 3: $14,000 remaining basis − $14,000 land absorbs remaining basis / = / 0
questions.explanationJa: 清算分配は原則として出資の払戻しで課税されず、パートナーのベーシスは分配資産に配分されて0になる。順序は現金、ホットアセット、その他の資産である。現金で$26,000−$12,000＝$14,000が残り、ホットアセットはないので、土地がこの残りのベーシスをすべて引き受ける。したがって土地のベーシスは帳簿価額$10,000ではなく$14,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.7

questions.stem: Curry's adjusted basis in Vantage Partnership was $5,000 at the time of receiving a nonliquidating distribution of land. The land had an adjusted basis of $6,000 and a fair market value of $9,000 to Vantage. What was the amount of Curry's basis in the land?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, because cash was not distributed, Curry's basis in Vantage Partnership is reduced by only the carried-over basis in the land. However, the land's carryover basis ($6,000) is limited to Curry's basis in Vantage Partnership ($5,000). Therefore, Curry's basis in the land is $5,000.
questions.explanationJa: 現金の分配はないので、ベーシスは土地の引継ぎ帳簿価額だけ減らされる。ただし、非清算分配で受け取る資産のベーシスはパートナーのベーシスを上限とするため、土地の帳簿価額$6,000はCurryのベーシス$5,000に制限される。よって土地のベーシスは$5,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.8

questions.stem: Each of the following statements describes a characteristic of both general partnerships and S corporations except

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both tax ordinary business income at the owner level.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both can be formed with nontaxable exchanges of property for an ownership interest.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both may have owners who work for the entity but must pay self-employment tax.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither tax ordinary business income at the entity level.

questions.explanation:
Partnerships and S corporations share some characteristics. For example, upon formation of either entity, owners can make a nontaxable contribution of cash and/or property to the entity in exchange for a percentage of ownership.

In addition, both entities are pass-through entities and are generally not subject to income tax at the entity level. Instead, entity income, deductions, and credits are passed through to the owners, and the entity income is taxed at the owner level.

Most owners of both types of entities are not subject to self-employment tax. However, a difference between the two entities arises when an owner actively participates in the entity's operation instead of being a passive investor. An S corporation owner participating in the S corporation's operation is classified as an employee and is subject to Social Security and Medicare taxes (FICA tax). Conversely, a general partner participating in the partnership's operation is not classified as an employee but is considered self-employed. Therefore, only general partners who actively participate in their partnerships' operations are subject to self-employment tax.
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップとS法人はいずれもパススルー事業体であり、事業所得はオーナー段階で課税され、事業体段階では課税されない。また、どちらも設立時に財産を拠出して持分を受け取る交換を非課税で行える。違いは事業に従事するオーナーの扱いで、S法人で働く株主は従業員としてFICA税（社会保障税・メディケア税）の対象となり、自営業者税の対象になるのは事業に従事するジェネラル・パートナーだけである。よって、両者に共通しないのは「事業に従事するオーナーが自営業者税を払う」という記述である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.9

questions.stem:
In the current year, a partnership reported the following items:

Fees earned | $500,000
Salary expense | 100,000
Utility expense | 5,000
Charitable contributions | 8,000
Long-term capital gain | 2,000
Office supplies | 500

What is the partnership's ordinary income?
questions.explanation:
A partnership is a form of pass-through entity that does not pay income taxes. Instead, partnerships must file an annual information return (Form 1065) and report ordinary income, losses, and separately stated items. Form 1065 also includes the allocation of those amounts to each partner in a Schedule K-1. Partners then include their Schedule K-1 amounts in their income tax returns.

The purpose of separately stating items is to allow for any special treatment on the individual partners' tax returns. As a result, any item that would be included in the gross income of a partner, without restrictions or limitations, is included in the partnership's ordinary income or loss calculation.

In this scenario, the partnership's ordinary income is calculated as follows:

Fees earned | $500,000
Salary expense | (100,000)
Utility expense | (5,000)
Office supplies | (500)
Partnership ordinary income | $394,500

("$386,500" / "$388,500" / "$396,500") The charitable contributions ($8,000) and long-term capital gain ($2,000) have special treatment on the partners' tax returns. Therefore, they are separately stated items that are not part of the ordinary business income calculation.
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップは自ら納税せず、通常の事業所得と個別記載項目を分けてパートナーに配分する。パートナー段階で制限や特別な扱いを受ける項目は個別記載となる。通常の所得は、報酬$500,000−給与$100,000−水道光熱費$5,000−事務用品$500＝$394,500である。寄附金$8,000と長期キャピタルゲイン$2,000はパートナーの申告で特別な扱いを受ける個別記載項目なので含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.10

questions.stem: Tally and Bailey form the Pelion Partnership. Tally contributed $175,000 for a 70% partnership interest. Bailey contributed land with a fair market value of $75,000 and an adjusted basis of $25,000 to the partnership in exchange for a 30% interest. The partnership assumed Bailey's $10,000 recourse mortgage on the land. What is Tally's basis in her partnership interest?
questions.explanation:
When a partnership (P/S) is created, the partners typically contribute cash and/or property in exchange for the partnership interest. Because the exchange is generally nontaxable, the basis of the property contributed by each partner carries over to the P/S.

Contributions of property increase a partner's basis in the P/S by the adjusted tax basis of the property at the time of the contribution. If the property is subject to a liability that is assumed by the P/S, the partner's adjusted tax basis is reduced by the liability. Because the partners may ultimately be responsible for P/S recourse debt, each partner's basis is increased by the partner's individual share of the liability the P/S has assumed.

In this scenario, Tally's basis (before the liability adjustment) for a 70% P/S interest equals the $175,000 contributed. However, because Bailey (the 30% partner) contributed land subject to a $10,000 recourse mortgage assumed by the P/S, Tally's share of the mortgage debt is $7,000 ($10,000 × 70%). Accordingly, Tally's basis is increased by $7,000, resulting in a basis of $182,000 ($175,000 + $7,000).
questions.explanationJa: 出資者のベーシスには、拠出した現金と財産の帳簿価額に加え、パートナーシップの負債のうち自分の持分相当額が加算される。Tallyは現金$175,000を拠出した。Baileyが持ち込んだ土地の$10,000のリコース抵当債務をパートナーシップが引き受けたので、Tallyの持分70%相当の$10,000×70%＝$7,000がベーシスに加わる。よってTallyのベーシスは$175,000＋$7,000＝$182,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.11

questions.stem: Molloy contributed $40,000 in cash in exchange for a one-third interest in the RST Partnership. In the first year of partnership operations, RST had taxable income of $60,000. In addition, Molloy received a $5,000 distribution of cash. At the end of the partnership year, the partnership had $18,000 in recourse debt and $24,000 in nonrecourse debt. What was Molloy's at-risk basis in RST at year end?
questions.explanation:
Unlike shareholders in a corporation, partners in a P/S do not have limited liability protection; therefore, the individual partners may be responsible (at risk) for the debts of the P/S. Increases in a partner's share of P/S liabilities (recourse, nonrecourse) are added to basis.

The at-risk rules prevent partners from deducting losses greater than their personal liabilities in the P/S. Therefore, the at-risk basis excludes P/S nonrecourse debt.

In this scenario, although Molloy's basis in the P/S is $69,000, the at-risk basis is only $61,000, as shown below:

Contribution | $40,000
Share of income ($60,000 × 1/3) | 20,000
Share of recourse debt ($18,000 × 1/3) | 6,000
Share of nonrecourse debt ($24,000 × 1/3) | 8,000
Distribution | (5,000)
P/S basis | $69,000
Less nonrecourse debt | (8,000)
At-risk basis | $61,000
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップの負債の持分相当額は、リコースかノンリコースかを問わずベーシスに加算される。ただしアットリスク額は、パートナーが個人的に負担しないノンリコース債務を除いて計算する。ベーシスは、出資$40,000＋所得の持分$60,000×1/3＝$20,000＋リコース債務$18,000×1/3＝$6,000＋ノンリコース債務$24,000×1/3＝$8,000−分配$5,000＝$69,000となる。ここからノンリコース分$8,000を除くと、アットリスク・ベーシスは$61,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.12

questions.stem: In Year 6 Albert, Berry, and Collins formed ABC Partnership. Collins, an active partner, contributed $20,000 in exchange for a 1/3 partnership interest. ABC had $30,000 in recourse debt and $12,000 in nonrecourse debt at the end of Year 6. The partnership sustained a loss of $150,000 in Year 6. How much of the loss is deductible for Collins?
questions.explanation:
Although Collins's basis in the P/S is $34,000, the at-risk basis is only $30,000. Collins's allocated loss is $50,000 ($150,000 × 1/3), but the deductible loss is limited to $30,000, the at-risk amount.

Cash contributed | $20,000
Share of P/S recourse debt (1/3 × $30,000) | 10,000
Share of P/S nonrecourse debt (1/3 × $12,000) | 4,000
Collins's P/S basis | $34,000
Less nonrecourse debt | (4,000)
Collins's at-risk basis | $30,000
questions.explanationJa: 損失の控除はアットリスク額が上限となり、アットリスク額にはノンリコース債務を含めない。Collinsのベーシスは、出資$20,000＋リコース債務$30,000×1/3＝$10,000＋ノンリコース債務$12,000×1/3＝$4,000＝$34,000である。ノンリコース分$4,000を除いたアットリスク額は$30,000となる。配分される損失は$150,000×1/3＝$50,000だが、控除できるのはアットリスク額の$30,000までである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.13

questions.stem: A partnership had four partners. Each partner contributed $100,000 cash. The partnership reported income of $80,000 for the year. During the year, each partner received $5,000 in guaranteed payments and $10,000 in distributions from the partnership. What was each partner's basis in the partnership at the end of the current year?
questions.explanation:
Guaranteed payments to partners are generally for services rendered or use of capital (salaries paid to partners). These payments are not treated as distributions. Instead, guaranteed payments are included as business expenses when determining the ordinary income or loss of the P/S and are reported as income by the partners.

In this scenario, each partner's beginning basis equals the $100,000 contributed to form the P/S. During the year, the P/S reported $80,000 net income ($20,000 to each partner) and paid each partner $5,000 in guaranteed payments (No adjustment to basis) and a $10,000 distribution. At year end, each partner's basis is $110,000.

Initial contribution | $100,000
P/S income (1/4 × $80,000) | 20,000
Distribution | (10,000)
Ending basis | $110,000
questions.explanationJa: パートナーへの保証支払（サービスの対価としての給与など）は分配ではなく、パートナーシップの事業費用として所得計算で控除され、受け取ったパートナーの所得となる。ベーシスの調整には使わない。各パートナーのベーシスは、出資$100,000＋所得の持分$80,000×1/4＝$20,000−分配$10,000＝$110,000である。保証支払$5,000はベーシスに影響しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.14

questions.stem: An individual is a 50% partner who materially participates in Stone Partnership. The individual's adjusted basis at the beginning of the year was $0. Stone had a $70,000 loss from its business. Stone borrowed $30,000 from a bank, of which $20,000 remained unpaid at year end. What amount of loss is the individual allowed in the current year from Stone?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the partner bears an economic risk of loss for the P/S bank loan. The loan balance at year end is $20,000. Accordingly, the partner's basis is increased by $10,000 ($20,000 × 50%). Because the beginning basis is $0, the basis before the partner's $35,000 loss ($70,000 × 50%) is $10,000. Because the basis cannot fall below $0, the partner deducts only $10,000 of the loss. The $25,000 ($35,000 − $10,000) suspended loss is carried forward until the partner has sufficient basis.

Beginning basis | $ 0
Share of P/S debt ($20,000 × 50%) | 10,000
Basis before loss | $10,000
Loss allowed | (10,000)
Basis at year end | $ 0
questions.explanationJa: このパートナーはパートナーシップの銀行借入について経済的な損失リスクを負うので、期末残高$20,000の持分50%、すなわち$10,000がベーシスに加わる。期首ベーシスは$0なので、損失控除前のベーシスは$10,000となる。損失の持分は$70,000×50%＝$35,000だが、ベーシスは0未満にならないため、当期に控除できる損失は$10,000である。残りの$25,000は繰り越され、ベーシスが十分になった年に控除する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.15

questions.stem:
A partner sold a 25% interest in a partnership for $400,000 cash plus assumption of the partner's share of the partnership liabilities. The following additional information relates to the partnership activities:

Partner's initial contribution: $ 100,000
Partnership income during the partner's ownership time period: 1,000,000
Partnership liabilities at date of sale: 60,000
Partner's cash withdrawals: 50,000

How much gain is recognized by the partner upon the sale of the partnership interest?
questions.explanation:
As in most sales, the recognized gain or loss on the sale of a partnership interest is calculated by subtracting the adjusted basis from the realized amount (net sales proceeds). The realized amount is the sum of all economic benefits received by the selling partner, including noncash benefits such as property. Noncash benefits also include debt relief, which is treated as cash received to immediately pay off the debt:

Cash received | $400,000
Property received (FMV) | 0
Debt assumed from partner (25% × $60,000) | 15,000
Realized amount | $415,000

The selling partner's basis is the sum of the partner's:

Contributions to partnership | $100,000
Allocated income (25% × $1,000,000) | 250,000
Allocated liabilities (25% × $60,000) | 15,000
Less: Distributions | (50,000)
Partner basis before sale | $315,000

Accordingly, the selling partner recognizes a $100,000 gain ($415,000 realized amount − $315,000 basis) on the sale of the partnership interest.

Note: The sale of a partnership interest should not be confused with a liquidating distribution.
questions.explanationJa: 持分売却の損益は、実現額から調整後ベーシスを引いて求める。負債の引受けによる債務免除も現金受領とみなして実現額に含める。実現額は、現金$400,000＋負債の持分25%×$60,000＝$15,000で$415,000となる。ベーシスは、出資$100,000＋所得の持分25%×$1,000,000＝$250,000＋負債の持分$15,000−引出し$50,000＝$315,000である。よって認識する利得は$415,000−$315,000＝$100,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.16

questions.stem: Smith received a one-third interest of a partnership by contributing $3,000 in cash, land, and a computer. The land has a fair market value of $5,000, and a cost of $2,000 and it is subject to a $900 mortgage. The computer has a fair market value of $2,000 and had an original cost of $2,500 and accumulated depreciation of $1,500. As a condition of the contribution, Smith paid off the mortgage on the land. Which of the following amounts represents Smith's basis in the partnership?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Smith contributes:

$3,000 cash.

Land costing $2,000 and subject to $900 mortgage that was paid off prior to the contribution. Therefore, no reduction is required to Smith's adjusted tax basis.

A computer with an adjusted tax basis of $1,000 ($2,500 cost − $1,500 accumulated depreciation).

Accordingly, Smith's basis in the partnership is $6,000 ($3,000 + $2,000 + $1,000).
questions.explanationJa: 財産の拠出によるベーシスは、時価ではなく調整後の税務上の帳簿価額で計算する。拠出したのは、現金$3,000、取得原価$2,000の土地、帳簿価額$1,000（原価$2,500−減価償却累計額$1,500）のコンピュータである。土地の抵当債務$900はSmithが拠出前に完済しているため、パートナーシップへの負債移転によるベーシスの減額はない。よってベーシスは$3,000＋$2,000＋$1,000＝$6,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.17

questions.stem:
In the current year, when Hoben's tax basis in Lynz Partnership interest was $10,000, Hoben received a liquidating distribution as follows:

Adjusted tax basis | Fair market value
Marketable securities | $ 5,000 | $ 5,000
Land | 25,000 | 27,000

Lynz had no appreciated inventory, unrealized receivables, or properties that had been contributed by its partners. What was Hoben's recognized gain on the distribution?
questions.explanation:
In general, a liquidating partnership distribution is a nontaxable return of a partner's capital. However, if cash and cash equivalents (fair market value [FMV] of marketable securities) distributions exceed a partner's basis in the partnership, the amount above basis is a taxable capital gain. Conversely, property distributions (hot assets, capital assets) that exceed basis (after accounting for cash distributions) are nontaxable when distributed. The property's basis assumes the partner's remaining basis in the partnership, deferring any gain or loss until the property is sold.

In this scenario, the distributed marketable securities' FMV ($5,000) did not exceed Hoben's basis in Lynz Partnership ($10,000), so Hoben recognized $0 gain.

Note: The land distribution had no effect on gain.
questions.explanationJa: 清算分配は原則として出資の払戻しで課税されず、利得が生じるのは現金および現金同等物（市場性ある有価証券は時価で現金扱い）がパートナーのベーシスを超える場合に限られる。有価証券の時価$5,000はHobenのベーシス$10,000を超えないので、認識する利得は$0である。土地は残りのベーシスを引き継ぐだけで、損益は売却時まで繰り延べられ、利得の計算には影響しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.18

questions.stem: Tucker received a partnership distribution of $20,000 cash and a building with an adjusted basis of $30,000 and a fair market value of $10,000. Tucker's basis in the partnership immediately prior to the distribution was $10,000. What is Tucker's basis (if any) in the building?
questions.explanation: Tucker's partnership basis of $10,000 is first reduced by the $20,000 cash distribution (but not below zero). This results in $0 basis and $10,000 ($20,000 − $10,000) taxable income. Since there is no remaining basis for the $30,000 building to offset, Tucker assumes a $0 basis in the building and any gain is deferred until the building is disposed of or sold
questions.explanationJa: 分配はまず現金でベーシスを減らすが、ベーシスは0未満にならない。ベーシス$10,000に対し現金$20,000が分配されるので、ベーシスは$0となり、超過分の$20,000−$10,000＝$10,000が課税される。残りのベーシスがないため、建物の帳簿価額$30,000は引き継げず、建物のベーシスは$0である。建物に係る利得は処分・売却時まで繰り延べられる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.19

questions.stem:
Slater Slopes is a newly formed ski resort partnership with a natural business year ending May 31. The ownership and tax years of its three partners are as follows:

Partner | Partnership Interest | Tax Year Ends
Sam Slater | 20% | December 31
Excelsior Enterprises | 40% | November 30
Pinnacle Productions | 40% | November 30

Which of the following is not an acceptable year end for Slater Slopes?
questions.explanation:
A partnership (P/S) generally must adopt the tax year used by the majority partners (partners owning >50% interest) if those partners have the same tax year.

In this scenario, Excelsior Enterprises and Pinnacle Productions have a majority interest of 80% (40% + 40%). Accordingly, the P/S has a required tax year of November 30. If the P/S wants a different tax year, it can provide a valid business reason (for May 31) or make a Section 444 election. This election allows the P/S to elect October 31, September 30, or August 31 (no more than three months prior to November 30) as a tax year. December 31 is not allowed because the tax year must be that of the majority interest, not a principal partner (Sam Slater).
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップは原則として、持分の過半（50%超）を持つパートナーが同じ課税年度を用いていれば、その年度を採用しなければならない。Excelsior EnterprisesとPinnacle Productionsが合わせて80%を持ち、どちらも11月30日決算なので、要求される課税年度は11月30日である。正当な事業上の理由があれば5月31日を、Section 444の選択をすれば11月30日から3か月以内の繰延べとなる10月31日・9月30日・8月31日を選べる。12月31日は過半の持分ではなくSam Slater（20%）の年度にすぎず、認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.20

questions.stem:
PDK, LLC had three members with equal ownership percentages. PDK elected to be treated as a partnership. For the tax year ending December 31, Year 1, PDK had the following income and expense items:

Revenues | $120,000
Interest income | 6,000
Gain on sale of securities | 8,000
Salaries | 36,000
Guaranteed payments | 10,000
Rent expense | 21,000
Depreciation expense | 18,000
Charitable contributions | 3,000

What would PDK report as non-separately stated income for Year 1 tax purposes?
questions.explanation:
Guaranteed payments refer to payments made to partners that are not based on income or loss. Instead, they are based on a contractual relationship (a salary) between the partner and the partnership. These payments represent an ordinary business expense and are therefore included in the calculation of partnership ordinary business income.

In this scenario, PDK, LLC's partnership non-separately stated income (ordinary business income) is calculated as:

Revenue | $120,000
Salaries | (36,000)
Guaranteed payments | (10,000)
Rent expense | (21,000)
Depreciation | (18,000)
Partnership non-separately stated income | $35,000

("$30,000" / "$43,000" / "$51,000") The interest income ($6,000), gain on sale of securities ($8,000), and charitable contributions ($3,000) have special treatment or are subject to special treatment on the partners' own tax returns. Therefore, they are separately stated items.

Note:
A partnership reports non-separately calculated (ordinary business) income/losses and separately stated items, which are allocated to the partners. Separately stated items (charitable contributions, capital gains/losses, interest revenue) are not part of ordinary business income/losses.
questions.explanationJa: 保証支払は所得・損失に連動しない契約上の支払（給与に相当）であり、通常の事業費用として非個別記載所得の計算で控除する。非個別記載所得は、収益$120,000−給与$36,000−保証支払$10,000−賃借料$21,000−減価償却費$18,000＝$35,000である。受取利息$6,000、有価証券売却益$8,000、寄附金$3,000はパートナーの申告で特別な扱いを受ける個別記載項目なので含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.21

questions.stem: Sutton is a partner of RST Partnership. RST distributed $3,000 cash and a building with an adjusted basis of $10,000 and a fair market value of $50,000 to Sutton. Before the distributions, Sutton's basis in the partnership was $90,000. What amount of these distributions is taxable to Sutton in the current year?
questions.explanation:
Nonliquidating partnership distributions are generally returns of capital and are not taxable to the partner. However, if cash distributions exceed a partner's basis in the partnership, the amount above basis is taxable income (a capital gain).

Distributions reduce a partner's basis (but not below zero). Basis is first reduced by cash distributions to determine any gain. Next, basis is reduced by the partnership's adjusted basis in distributed property. If the partnership's adjusted basis exceeds the partner's basis (after cash distributions), the partner does not recognize a gain. Instead, the partner's basis in the property is limited to the available basis.

In this scenario, Sutton must reduce the basis in RST Partnership first by the $3,000 cash distribution. Because the cash distribution does not exceed Sutton's $90,000 basis, the distribution is nontaxable ($0 taxable). Sutton's basis is further reduced by the partnership's adjusted basis ($10,000) in the distributed land, which has no effect on taxable income.
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配は原則として出資の払戻しで課税されず、課税されるのは現金の分配がパートナーのベーシスを超える場合だけである。Suttonのベーシス$90,000を、まず現金$3,000で減らすが、ベーシスを超えないので課税額は$0となる。続いて建物のパートナーシップ帳簿価額$10,000でベーシスを減らすが、資産の分配は課税所得に影響しない。よって当期に課税される金額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.22

questions.stem:
The adjusted basis of Smith's interest in EVA Partnership was $230,000 immediately before receiving the following distribution in complete liquidation of EVA:

Basis to EVA | Fair market value
Cash | $150,000 | $150,000
Real estate | $120,000 | $146,000

What is Smith's basis in the real estate?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Smith's basis in the real estate is $80,000, as shown below.

Remaining basis in EVA:
Step 1: $230,000 Smith's basis in EVA Partnership − $150,000 cash / = / $80,000
Step 2: $80,000 remaining basis − $0 hot assets / = / 80,000
Step 3: $80,000 remaining basis − $80,000 real estate absorbs remaining basis / = / 0
questions.explanationJa: 清算分配では、パートナーのベーシスを現金、ホットアセット、その他の資産の順に配分して0にする。現金$150,000でベーシスは$230,000−$150,000＝$80,000となる。ホットアセットはないので、不動産が残りのベーシス$80,000をすべて引き受ける。よって不動産のベーシスは、帳簿価額$120,000や時価$146,000ではなく$80,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.23

questions.stem: In a liquidating distribution, the CSU Partnership distributed to each partner cash of $4,000, inventory with a basis of $4,000 and a fair market value (FMV) of $6,000, and land with an adjusted basis of $5,000 and an FMV of $3,000. Partner Chang's outside basis in the partnership was $12,000 on the date of the distribution. In the following year, Chang sold the inventory for $5,000 and the land for $3,000. What income must Chang report upon the sale of these assets?
questions.explanation:
A partner's outside basis is reduced to $0 by allocating the basis to the distributed assets in the following order: cash, unrealized receivables and inventory, and all other assets (land). Generally, the assets have a carryover basis (not FMV) from the P/S. When required, carryover basis is adjusted to absorb any remaining outside basis in the P/S.

In this case, the liquidating distribution results in no gain or loss. Chang's outside basis is reduced by the $4,000 cash and then by the $4,000 carryover basis of the inventory. Because basis may never go below $0, the remaining outside basis (not the $5,000 carryover basis) of $4,000 ($12,000 − $4,000 cash − $4,000 inventory) is allocated to the land.

When the assets are sold, bases of $4,000 for inventory and $4,000 for land are used to determine gain or loss. Because inventory generates ordinary income, any gain or loss will be ordinary. However, because land is a capital asset, a capital gain (loss) results. Chang has a $1,000 ordinary gain and $1,000 capital loss, calculated as follows:

Inventory: $5,000 sales price − $4,000 basis = $1,000 ordinary gain
Land: $3,000 sales price − $4,000 basis = $1,000 capital loss
questions.explanationJa: 清算分配では、外部ベーシスを現金、未実現債権・棚卸資産、その他の資産（土地）の順に配分し、その他の資産のベーシスは残りの外部ベーシスに合わせて調整される。外部ベーシス$12,000から現金$4,000と棚卸資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額$4,000を引いた残り$4,000が、土地のベーシスとなる（帳簿価額$5,000ではない）。分配時点の損益はない。翌年の売却では、棚卸資産は$5,000−$4,000＝$1,000の通常利得、土地は資本資産なので$3,000−$4,000＝$1,000のキャピタルロスとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.24

questions.stem: The adjusted basis of Jones' partnership interest was $50,000 immediately before Jones received a current distribution of $20,000 cash and property with an adjusted basis to the partnership of $40,000 and a fair market value of $35,000. What is Jones' basis in the distributed property?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the cash distribution reduces Jones' basis in the partnership to $30,000 ($50,000 beginning basis − $20,000 cash). Jones' basis is further reduced by the property's basis. The property's carryover basis ($40,000), however, is limited to Jones' $30,000 remaining basis. Therefore, Jones' basis in the property is $30,000.
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配では、まず現金でベーシスを減らし、次に資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額で減らす。資産のベーシスは残りのベーシスが上限となる。現金$20,000でJonesのベーシスは$50,000−$20,000＝$30,000となる。資産の帳簿価額$40,000は残りのベーシス$30,000に制限されるので、資産のベーシスは$30,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.25

questions.stem: Turner, Reed, and Sumner are equal partners in TRS partnership. Turner contributed land with an adjusted basis of $20,000 and a fair market value (FMV) of $50,000. Reed contributed equipment with an adjusted basis of $40,000 and an FMV of $50,000. Sumner provided services worth $50,000. What amount of income is recognized as a result of the transfers?
questions.explanation:
Contributions (cash, property) to a partnership (P/S) in exchange for a P/S interest generally result in no gain or loss recognized by the partner. A partner may also perform personal services (legal, accounting) in exchange for an interest in a P/S. The personal services are valued at the FMV of the P/S interest received.

When the exchange of personal services occurs, it is treated as if the P/S paid the partner for the services performed. Accordingly, the partner recognizes income equal to the FMV of the P/S interest. FMV of the interest is used because that is what the partner would receive in a liquidating P/S distribution.

In this scenario, Turner, Reed, and Sumner are equal partners, each receiving a P/S interest with FMV of $50,000. Turner and Reed contributed property in exchange for their P/S interests; therefore, no gain is recognized. Because Sumner contributed services, $50,000 is reported as income.

Note: Although the value of services and FMV of P/S interest are the same in this scenario, the FMV of P/S interest is always used to determine the income reported.
questions.explanationJa: 現金や財産を拠出してパートナーシップ持分を受け取っても、原則として損益は認識しない。一方、サービスを提供して持分を受け取った場合は、パートナーシップから報酬を受けたものとみなされ、受け取った持分の時価相当額が所得となる。TurnerとReedは財産の拠出なので利得を認識せず、サービスを提供したSumnerだけが持分の時価$50,000を所得として計上する。よって認識される所得は$50,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.26

questions.stem: Campbell acquired a 10% interest in Vogue Partnership by contributing a building with an adjusted basis of $40,000 and a fair market value of $90,000. The building was subject to a $60,000 mortgage that was assumed by Vogue. The other partners contributed cash only. The basis of Campbell's partnership interest in Vogue is:
questions.explanation:
If the property is subject to a liability (mortgage) assumed by the P/S, the contributing partner's basis is reduced by the liability. Because the partners may ultimately be responsible for P/S debt, each partner's basis is increased by their pro rata share of the new P/S liability.

However, if the property has a liability exceeding its adjusted tax basis, a negative basis could be created for the contributing partner. If this occurs, that partner will recognize a capital gain equal to the required adjustment to bring the basis up to $0.

In this scenario, Campbell contributed a building subject to a mortgage that exceeded the property's adjusted tax basis, thus creating a negative basis for Campbell. Because a partner's basis in the P/S cannot be negative, the basis is increased to $0 and Campbell recognizes a $14,000 gain.

Campbell's basis in contributed building | $40,000
Less: mortgage assumed by P/S | (60,000)
Plus: Campbell's 10% share P/S mortgage | 6,000
Basis before adjustment for gain | ($14,000)
Capital gain recognized | $14,000
Campbell's basis in P/S | $0
questions.explanationJa: 負債付きの財産を拠出してパートナーシップが負債を引き受けると、拠出者のベーシスは引き受けられた負債の額だけ減り、パートナーシップ負債の自分の持分相当額だけ増える。計算は、建物の帳簿価額$40,000−抵当債務$60,000＋持分10%×$60,000＝$6,000で、ベーシスは−$14,000となる。ベーシスはマイナスにならないため、$14,000のキャピタルゲインを認識してベーシスを$0に戻す。よってCampbellのベーシスは$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.27

questions.stem: Owen's tax basis in Regal Partnership was $8,000 at the time Owen received a nonliquidating distribution of $3,000 cash and land with an adjusted basis of $7,000 to Regal and a fair market value of $9,000. Regal did not have unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory, or properties that had been contributed by its partners. What was Owen's tax basis in the property received?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Owen received cash and property. Following the ordering rules, the $3,000 cash reduces Owen's P/S basis to $5,000 ($8,000 basis − $3,000). Although the property has a carryover basis of $7,000, the basis is limited to the remaining $5,000 basis in the P/S
questions.explanationJa: 現金、その他の資産の順にベーシスを減らすルールに従う。現金$3,000でOwenのベーシスは$8,000−$3,000＝$5,000となる。土地の引継ぎ帳簿価額は$7,000だが、非清算分配で受け取る資産のベーシスは残りのベーシスが上限なので、土地のベーシスは$5,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.28

questions.stem:
On May 1, Year 1, Jones and Curry formed Major Partnership as equal partners by contributing the assets below:

Asset | Adjusted tax basis | Fair market value
Jones | Cash | $45,000 | $45,000
Curry | Land | 30,000 | 57,000

The partnership incurred $8,000 of recourse debt and $12,000 of nonrecourse debt on May 2. What were Curry's tax basis and at-risk basis in the partnership interest on May 2, Year 1?
Tax basis | At-risk basis
questions.explanation:
Contributions of property increase the contributing partner's basis in the P/S by the property's adjusted tax basis (not FMV) at the time of the contribution. Because partners do not have limited liability protection, the individual partners may ultimately be responsible for the P/S debts. Each partner's basis is increased by their individual share of P/S liabilities (recourse, nonrecourse).

At-risk rules prevent partners from deducting losses greater than the amount of their personal liability (economic risk of loss from recourse debt) in the P/S. Nonrecourse liabilities (secured by collateral) provide basis for distributions but generally do not provide basis for deducting losses because the partners do not bear the risk for the loss. Therefore, the at-risk basis excludes P/S nonrecourse debt.

Although Curry's tax basis is $40,000, the at-risk basis is only $34,000; the $6,000 difference is the nonrecourse debt.

Land contributed (adjusted tax basis) | $30,000
Share of recourse debt (50% × $8,000) | 4,000
Share of nonrecourse debt (50% × $12,000) | 6,000
Curry's tax basis | $40,000
Less: Nonrecourse debt | (6,000)
Curry's at-risk basis | $34,000
questions.explanationJa: 財産を拠出した場合のベーシスは、時価ではなく調整後の税務上の帳簿価額で計算し、パートナーシップ負債の持分相当額（リコース・ノンリコースとも）を加える。アットリスク額は、パートナーが損失リスクを負わないノンリコース債務を除く。Curryの税務ベーシスは、土地$30,000＋リコース債務50%×$8,000＝$4,000＋ノンリコース債務50%×$12,000＝$6,000＝$40,000である。そこからノンリコース分$6,000を除いたアットリスク・ベーシスは$34,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.29

questions.stem: The adjusted basis of a taxpayer's partnership interest was $50,000 immediately before the taxpayer received a current distribution of $20,000 cash and property with an adjusted basis to the partnership of $40,000 and a fair market value of $35,000. What is the taxpayer's basis in the distributed property?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the taxpayer must reduce the basis in the partnership first by the $20,000 cash distribution ($30,000 remaining basis = $50,000 starting basis − $20,000 cash). The taxpayer's basis in the partnership is further reduced by the partnership's adjusted basis in the property. However, the property's $40,000 carryover basis is limited to the partner's $30,000 remaining basis. Therefore, the partner's basis in the property is $30,000.
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配では、まず現金でベーシスを減らし、次に資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額で減らす。資産のベーシスは残りのベーシスが上限となる。現金$20,000でベーシスは$50,000−$20,000＝$30,000となる。資産の帳簿価額$40,000は残りのベーシス$30,000に制限されるので、資産のベーシスは$30,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.30

questions.stem:
J and K formed a general partnership by contributing $10,000 each. The partnership incurred a loss of $30,000 in Year 1, income of $6,000 in Year 2, and income of $10,000 in Year 3. What is the adjusted basis for tax purposes of each partner's interest in the partnership at the end of each year?
Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, J and K each contributed $10,000 for their partnership interests. Absent additional information, the partners share the partnership's income or loss 50/50. The adjusted basis of each partner's interest at the end of each year is $0, $0, and $3,000, calculated as follows:

Partner basis | Suspended loss balance
Contribution | $10,000
Year 1 loss (50%) | (15,000)
Adjusted basis, Year 1 | $ 0 | ($5,000)
Year 2 income (50%) | 3,000
Less Year 1 carryover loss | (3,000) | 3,000
Adjusted basis, Year 2 | $ 0 | ($2,000)
Year 3 income (50%) | 5,000
Less Year 1 carryover loss | (2,000) | 2,000
Adjusted basis, Year 3 | $ 3,000 | $0

Note:
A partner's basis in their partnership interest may never fall below zero. Any excess loss over basis that is suspended (disallowed) is carried forward to future years and deducted when the partner has sufficient basis to absorb the loss.
questions.explanationJa: 特段の定めがないので、JとKは損益を50%ずつ負担する。ベーシスは0未満にならず、超過する損失は繰り越して、ベーシスが生じた年に控除する。1年目は$10,000−損失$15,000でベーシス$0、繰越損失$5,000となる。2年目は所得$3,000を繰越損失$3,000で相殺してベーシス$0（繰越損失残り$2,000）となる。3年目は所得$5,000から繰越損失$2,000を控除してベーシス$3,000となるので、各年末のベーシスは$0、$0、$3,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.31

questions.stem: On January 4, Year 4, Smith and White contributed $4,000 and $6,000 in cash, respectively, and formed the Macro General Partnership. The partnership agreement allocated profits and losses 40% to Smith and 60% to White. In Year 4, Macro purchased property from an unrelated seller for $10,000 cash and a $40,000 mortgage note that was the liability of the partnership. What affect does Macro's liability have on Smith's tax basis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Has no effect on Smith's tax basis.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, Smith is a 40% ($4,000 / $10,000) partner and liable for 40% of the P/S debt. Therefore, the $40,000 mortgage incurred by the P/S increases Smith's tax basis by $16,000 (40% × $40,000).
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップの負債は、パートナーの負担割合に応じて各パートナーのベーシスを増やす。Smithは損益の40%を負担するパートナー（出資も$4,000÷$10,000＝40%）なので、パートナーシップの抵当債務$40,000の40%を負う。よってSmithの税務ベーシスは40%×$40,000＝$16,000増加する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.32

questions.stem:
Belson and Forman decided to terminate North Partnership. On the date of termination, North's balance sheet was as follows:

Adjusted basis:
Cash | $2,000
Equipment (fair market value $4,000) | 6,000
Capital--Belson | 4,000
Capital--Forman | 4,000

Forman's outside basis is $2,000. The partnership assets were distributed equally between the partners. What is Forman's tax basis in the property received?
questions.explanation:
The basis in a partnership is reduced in the following order:

Cash (In this scenario, $2,000 Forman's basis in North Partnership − $1,000 50% of cash = $1,000 remaining basis.)

Hot assets (No hot assets were distributed; Forman's remaining basis is $1,000.)

Other property assumes the partner's remaining basis in the partnership. (The distributed equipment assumes Forman's remaining $1,000 basis in North regardless of North's carryover basis in the equipment.)
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップのベーシスは、現金、ホットアセット、その他の資産の順に減らす。資産は均等に分配されるので、Formanが受け取る現金は$2,000の50%＝$1,000であり、外部ベーシス$2,000−$1,000＝$1,000が残る。ホットアセットの分配はない。設備は、パートナーシップの帳簿価額にかかわらず残りのベーシス$1,000を引き継ぐので、受け取った財産のベーシスは$1,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.33

questions.stem: Dean is a 25% partner in Target Partnership. Dean's tax basis in Target on January 1, Year 4, was $20,000. At the end of Year 4, Dean received nonliquidating distributions of $8,000 and property with an adjusted tax basis of $2,000 and fair market value of $6,000 from Target. For Year 4, Target reported ordinary business income of $40,000 and recourse debt of $12,000. What was Dean's tax basis in Target on December 31, Year 4?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Dean, a 25% partner, had a beginning basis of $20,000. The basis is increased for 25% of the P/S business income and recourse debt. It is decreased for the $8,000 distribution and $2,000 (adjusted tax basis) of the property distributed. At year end, Dean's tax basis is $23,000, as shown below.

Beginning basis: $20,000
Plus: Share of P/S income (25% × $40,000): 10,000
Plus: Share of recourse debt (25% × $12,000): 3,000
Less: Cash distribution: (8,000)
Less: Property distribution (P/S adjusted basis): (2,000)
Ending basis: $23,000
questions.explanationJa: 期首ベーシス$20,000に、通常事業所得の持分25%×$40,000＝$10,000と、リコース債務の持分25%×$12,000＝$3,000を加える。そこから現金の分配$8,000と、分配された資産のパートナーシップ帳簿価額$2,000（時価$6,000ではない）を差し引く。よって期末ベーシスは$20,000＋$10,000＋$3,000−$8,000−$2,000＝$23,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.34

questions.stem: Danson and Ellerby are equal partners in DE Partnership, which is in the business of selling fine art. DE owns assets with a tax basis and fair market value of $240,000. In January of the current year, Finley contributes to the partnership some personal investment art with a fair market value of $120,000 (tax basis $80,000) to become a one-third partner in the new DEF Partnership. In October of the current year, DEF sells the art received from Finley for $141,000. What amount of gain from the sale of the artwork should be allocated to Finley?
questions.explanation:
If the asset contributed is appreciated property (ie, the fair market value exceeds the property's basis), any excess fair market value is considered built-in gain (pre-contribution gain).

If built-in gain property is disposed of by the partnership, special allocation rules apply to prevent the contributing partner from shifting any pre-contribution gain to the other partners. The lesser of the recognized gain or the built-in gain is allocated to the contributing partner. Any remaining gain is allocated among all the partners. Finley will be allocated $47,000 of the gain from the sale.

Partnership's recognized gain ($141,000 - $80,000): $61,000
Built-in gain allocated to Finley ($120,000 - $80,000): (40,000)
Balance allocated to all partners: $21,000
Finley's share of balance ($21,000 x 1/3): $7,000
Finley's total allocated gain ($40,000 + $7,000): $47,000
questions.explanationJa: 含み益のある財産を拠出した場合、時価が帳簿価額を超える部分は拠出前の含み益（ビルトイン・ゲイン）となる。パートナーシップがその財産を売却したときは、含み益を他のパートナーに移さないよう、認識した利得とビルトイン・ゲインのいずれか小さい額を拠出者に配分し、残りを全パートナーで分ける。認識利得は$141,000−$80,000＝$61,000、ビルトイン・ゲインは$120,000−$80,000＝$40,000である。残り$21,000の3分の1の$7,000を加え、Finleyへの配分は$40,000＋$7,000＝$47,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.35

questions.stem:
Osha, a cash-basis calendar-year partnership, began business on April 1, Year 5. Osha incurred and paid the following during Year 5:

Legal services associated with formation of the partnership: $15,260
Accounting fees associated with promoting and selling partnership interests: 10,000

Osha elected to amortize costs. What is the maximum amount of organizational costs deductible on Osha's Year 5 partnership return?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the partnership has elected to amortize (not capitalize) the organizational costs. The $15,260 for legal services qualify as organizational expenses. However, the $10,000 fees for promoting and selling partnership interests do not. Because the operations began on April 1, the maximum amount deductible in Year 5 is $5,513, as calculated below.

Immediate deduction | $5,000
Amortization [($15,260 − $5,000) × 9/180]* | 513
Total | $5,513
*Operations began April 1, so 9 months of amortization allowed:
questions.explanationJa: 設立に関する法務費用$15,260は組織費に当たるが、持分の募集・販売に関する会計報酬$10,000は組織費に当たらない。償却を選択した場合、組織費のうち$5,000を即時に控除でき、残額は180か月で償却する。事業開始は4月1日なので、5年目の償却は9か月分の($15,260−$5,000)×9/180＝$513となる。よって最大控除額は$5,000＋$513＝$5,513である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.36

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 7, Kane was a 25% equal partner in Maze General Partnership, which had partnership liabilities of $300,000. On January 2, Year 7, a new partner was admitted, and Kane's interest was reduced to 20%. On April 1, Year 7, Maze repaid a $100,000 general partnership loan. Ignoring any income, loss, or distribution for Year 7, what was the total effect of the two transactions on Kane's tax basis in Maze partnership interest?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, when the new partner is admitted, Kane's P/S interest decreased 5% (from 25% to 20%). This reduces Kane's share of the original P/S debt by $15,000 (5% × $300,000). When the P/S debt is decreased by $100,000 during the year, Kane's 20% share is $20,000 (20% × $100,000). Both reductions in liabilities are treated as distributions when calculating basis. Therefore, Kane's basis is decreased by $35,000 ($15,000 + $20,000).
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップ負債の持分が減ると、その減少額は分配とみなされてベーシスを減らす。新パートナーの加入でKaneの持分が25%から20%に下がったので、負債$300,000に対する持分が5%×$300,000＝$15,000減る。さらにパートナーシップが$100,000を返済したことで、Kaneの20%持分相当額$20,000が減る。合計でベーシスは$15,000＋$20,000＝$35,000減少する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.37

questions.stem:
A partner receives the following as part of a liquidating distribution:

Basis | FMV
Cash | $12,000 | $12,000
Accounts receivable (A/R) | 0 | 4,000
Land | 8,000 | 3,000
Total | $20,000 | $19,000

The partner's basis in the partnership immediately prior to the distribution is $25,000. What is the partner's basis in the A/R and the land immediately after the liquidating distribution?
questions.explanation:
Liquidating distributions have the following ordering rules:

Cash is distributed first, followed by unrealized receivables and then inventory. The partner's basis in these assets is always equal to the partnership's basis in these assets (carryover basis). Because unrealized receivables have not been reported as income (cash basis accounting), they have a $0 basis.

Any remaining partner basis is allocated to other property (land, equipment) received.

In this scenario, there is liquidating distribution of the partner's $25,000 interest. Following the ordering rules, the partner reduces basis by the $12,000 cash received and then by the A/R. The partner has a $0 basis in the A/R because the P/S had $0 basis in A/R. The remaining $13,000 ($25,000 P/S basis − $12,000 cash − $0 basis in A/R), not the carryover basis, is the partner's basis in land received
questions.explanationJa: 清算分配では、現金、未実現債権、棚卸資産の順に配分し、これらのベーシスは常にパートナーシップの帳簿価額を引き継ぐ。現金主義では売掛金はまだ所得計上されていないため、帳簿価額は$0である。ベーシス$25,000から現金$12,000と売掛金$0を引いた残り$13,000は、その他の資産である土地にすべて配分される。よって売掛金のベーシスは$0、土地のベーシスは帳簿価額$8,000ではなく$13,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.38

questions.stem:
On June 1, Year 4, a partner contributed $50,000 cash and equipment with an adjusted tax basis of $25,000 and a fair market value of $35,000 in exchange for a 50% interest in the B&B partnership's capital and profits. B&B partnership had existing $20,000 recourse debt and $16,000 nonrecourse debt on June 1. What is the tax basis and at-risk basis for the partner's interest in the B&B partnership on June 1, Year 4?
Tax basis | At-risk basis
questions.explanation:
Each partner's basis is increased by their individual share of P/S liabilities (eg, recourse, nonrecourse).

At-risk rules prevent partners from deducting losses greater than the amount of their personal liability in the P/S. Nonrecourse liabilities (liabilities secured by collateral) provide basis for distributions but generally do not provide basis for deducting losses because the partners do not bear the risk for the loss. Therefore, the at-risk basis excludes P/S nonrecourse debt.

Although the partner's basis in the P/S is $93,000, the at-risk basis is only $85,000; the $8,000 difference is the nonrecourse debt.

Cash contributed | $50,000
Equipment contributed (adjusted tax basis) | 25,000
Share of recourse debt (50% × $20,000) | 10,000
Share of nonrecourse debt (50% × $16,000) | 8,000
Partner's tax basis | $93,000
Less: nonrecourse debt | (8,000)
Partner's at-risk basis | $85,000
questions.explanationJa: パートナーのベーシスは、拠出した現金と財産の帳簿価額に、パートナーシップ負債の持分相当額（リコース・ノンリコースとも）を加えて計算する。アットリスク額からはノンリコース債務を除く。税務ベーシスは、現金$50,000＋設備の帳簿価額$25,000＋リコース債務50%×$20,000＝$10,000＋ノンリコース債務50%×$16,000＝$8,000＝$93,000である。ノンリコース分$8,000を除いたアットリスク・ベーシスは$85,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.39

questions.stem: Dale was a 50% partner in D&P Partnership. Dale contributed $10,000 in cash upon the formation of the partnership. D&P borrowed $10,000 to purchase equipment. During the first year of operations, D&P had $15,000 net taxable income, $2,000 tax-exempt interest income, a $3,000 distribution to each partner, and a $4,000 reduction of debt. At the end of the first year of operation, what amount would be Dale's basis?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Dale has a beginning basis of $10,000 (cash contribution). Because Dale has a 50% interest in the P/S, the basis is increased by half of the P/S liabilities, net taxable income, and tax-exempt interest income. Basis is decreased by the distribution and pro rata reduction of P/S liabilities. At the end of the year, Dale's basis is $18,500, as calculated below:

Beginning basis: $10,000
Share of liabilities ($10,000 × 50%): 5,000
Share of net income ($15,000 × 50%): 7,500
Share of tax-exempt income ($2,000 × 50%): 1,000
Distribution: (3,000)
Share of reduction in liabilities ($4,000 × 50%): (2,000)
Ending basis: $18,500
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.40

questions.stem: Partner A's basis in partnership ABC is $5,000 at the beginning of the year. During the year, Partner A received a nonliquidating distribution of $3,000 cash and property with an adjusted basis of $4,000 and fair market value of $5,000. What was Partner A's basis in the property received?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the cash distribution reduces Partner A's basis in ABC Partnership to $2,000 ($5,000 beginning basis − $3,000 cash). Partner A's basis is further reduced by the property's basis. However, the property's carryover basis ($4,000) is limited to Partner A's $2,000 remaining basis. Therefore, Partner A's basis in the property is $2,000.
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配では、まず現金でベーシスを減らし、次に資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額で減らす。資産のベーシスは残りのベーシスが上限となる。現金$3,000でPartner Aのベーシスは$5,000−$3,000＝$2,000となる。資産の帳簿価額$4,000は残りのベーシス$2,000に制限されるので、資産のベーシスは$2,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.41

questions.stem:
Jetson and Tomson are equal partners in JT Partnership, which has the following income and expense items:

Sales | $100,000
Interest income from checking account | 1,000
Charitable contributions | 3,000
Employee wages | 4,000
Cost of goods sold | 50,000

What is the nonseparately stated partnership income?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the $3,000 charitable contributions and the $1,000 interest income are separately stated items and are not part of P/S ordinary business income. The deduction for charitable contributions is subject to AGI limitations at the taxpayer level. Interest income is considered investment income and is required for the calculation of the investment interest limitation and the net investment income tax at the taxpayer level.

The remaining items are used in the calculation of $46,000 nonseparately stated business income for the P/S.

Sales | $100,000)
Employee wages | (4,000)
Cost of goods sold | (50,000)
Nonseparately stated P/S income | $46,000
questions.explanationJa: 寄附金$3,000はパートナー段階でAGIによる控除制限を受け、当座預金の受取利息$1,000は投資所得として投資利息の控除制限や純投資所得税の計算に使うため、どちらも個別記載項目となる。残りの項目で計算すると、非個別記載所得は売上$100,000−従業員給与$4,000−売上原価$50,000＝$46,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.42

questions.stem: The holding period of a partnership interest acquired in exchange for a contributed capital asset begins on the date

choices.label: A
choices.text: The partner is admitted into the partnership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partner transfers the asset to the partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The partner's holding period of the capital asset began.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The partner is first credited with the proportionate share of partnership capital.

questions.explanation: When a partner acquires a partnership interest (an asset) by contributing capital assets or Section 1231 property to the partnership, the contributed property's holding period prior to the exchange tacks on to the partnership interest. Therefore, the partnership interest assumes the contributed property's beginning date. However, the holding period of a partnership interest begins the day after an exchange when cash and other current assets (inventory, receivables) are contributed.
questions.explanationJa: 資本資産やSection 1231資産を拠出して持分を取得した場合、拠出前の資産の保有期間が持分の保有期間に通算される。したがって持分の保有期間は、パートナーがその資本資産を保有し始めた日から始まる。なお、現金や棚卸資産・債権などの流動資産を拠出した場合は、交換の翌日から保有期間が始まる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.43

questions.stem:
Which of the following should be used in computing the basis of a partner's interest acquired from another partner?
Cash paid by transferee to transferor | Transferee's share of partnership liabilities
questions.explanation:
In a partnership, each partner has a tax basis that is used to determine the deductibility of partnership losses and the treatment of partnership distributions. A partner's basis is not identical to the partner's equity or capital in the business. The basis includes the partner's share of partnership liabilities to creditors, and the partner's capital account does not.

For tax purposes, the beginning basis amount is equal to the partner's cash contribution to the partnership. However, if the partner acquired the partnership interest from another partner, generally the beginning basis is equal to the amount paid by the acquiring (transferee) partner to the selling (transferor) partner. In addition, the new partner's basis is increased by that partner's share of partnership liabilities.

This basis is adjusted each accounting period for the partner's share of partnership profits (losses), changes in partnership liabilities, additional contributions made, and distributions received. The basis may never fall below zero.
questions.explanationJa: 他のパートナーから持分を取得した場合、当初のベーシスは原則として、取得者が売却パートナーに支払った金額となる。さらに、取得したパートナーのベーシスには、パートナーシップ負債のうち自分の持分相当額が加算される。よって、支払った現金と、取得者が負担するパートナーシップ負債の持分の両方をベーシスの計算に用いる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.44

questions.stem:
On January 1, the partners' interest in capital, profits, and losses of Studio Partnership were

Partners | Percentages
Ross | 15%
Stone | 35%
Taylor | 50%

On April 9, Stone sold his entire interest to Taylor. For tax purposes, which of the following statements is correct regarding Studio's status as a partnership?
questions.explanation:
Studio did not terminate because there was no agreement to dissolve, no winding up of business, and no distribution of property to the partners. Studio will continue as the same tax entity (same federal identification number) with the two remaining partners (Ross and Taylor).

The new law repealed the rule that a partnership was terminated for tax purposes when 50% or more of the partnership interests changed hands within a 12-month period.
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップが税務上終了するのは事業が営まれなくなった場合であり、本問では解散の合意も清算も財産の分配もない。StudioはRossとTaylorの2名で、同じ課税主体（同じ連邦納税者番号）として存続するので、終了していない。12か月以内に50%以上の持分が移転すると終了するという旧ルールは廃止されている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.45

questions.stem:
Guaranteed payments made by a partnership to partners for services rendered to the partnership, that are deductible business expenses under the Internal Revenue Code, are
I. Deductible expenses in computing partnership income (loss)
II. Taxed as ordinary income to the partner receiving them
I | II
questions.explanation: Guaranteed payments are included in the receiving partner's personal ordinary income; however, they are not used in the calculation of the partner's tax basis in the partnership. The payments must be separately stated on the Schedule K-1 of each partner receiving such payments so that the partners include the income received on their individual tax returns.
questions.explanationJa: サービスの対価としての保証支払は、パートナーシップの所得（損失）の計算で事業費用として控除される。受け取ったパートナーは、これを個人の通常所得として課税される。そのため、保証支払は各パートナーのSchedule K-1に個別に記載され、パートナーは自分の申告に含める。なお、保証支払はパートナーのベーシスの計算には用いない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.46

questions.stem: Pert contributed land with a fair market value of $20,000 to a new partnership in exchange for a 50% partnership interest. The land had an adjusted basis of $12,000 to Pert and was subject to a $4,000 mortgage, which the partnership assumed. The partnership incurred a net loss of $22,000. At year end, what is the adjusted basis of Pert's partnership interest?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Pert contributed land subject to a mortgage assumed by the P/S. During the year, the P/S incurred a $22,000 loss. Because Pert's share of the loss would create a negative basis, only $10,000 of loss is allowed, resulting in a $0 basis at year end.

Contribution ($12,000 basis − $4,000 mortgage assumed): $8,000
Share of P/S mortgage (50% × $4,000): 2,000
Basis before loss: 10,000
Share of P/S loss ($22,000 × 50% = $11,000): (10,000)*
Basis at year end: $0
*Pert has $1,000 ($11,000 − $10,000) carryforward loss:
questions.explanationJa: Pertの拠出によるベーシスは、土地の帳簿価額$12,000からパートナーシップが引き受けた抵当債務$4,000を引いて$8,000となり、負債の持分50%×$4,000＝$2,000を加えて損失控除前は$10,000となる。損失の持分は$22,000×50%＝$11,000だが、ベーシスは0未満にならないため、認められるのは$10,000までである。よって期末ベーシスは$0で、$1,000の損失が繰り越される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.47

questions.stem: Partner A has a 40% interest in ABC partnership, with a basis of $40,000. ABC increased its liabilities by $125,000. What is Partner A's basis in ABC as a result of the increase in liabilities?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Partner A owns 40% of the partnership with a basis of $40,000. Because the partnership's liabilities increased by $125,000, the partner's basis is increased by $50,000 (40% × $125,000). Accordingly, Partner A's basis is $90,000 ($40,000 + $50,000).
questions.explanationJa: パートナーシップ負債が増えると、各パートナーのベーシスは持分割合に応じて増加する。Partner Aは40%持分なので、負債の増加$125,000のうち40%×$125,000＝$50,000がベーシスに加わる。よってベーシスは$40,000＋$50,000＝$90,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.48

questions.stem:
Acme Partnership reported the following items of income and expense:

Sales | $200,000
Cost of goods sold | 115,000
Interest expense on bank line of credit | 13,000
Charitable contributions | 2,000
Administrative expenses | 50,000
Long-term capital gain | 10,000

What amount should be reported as ordinary income?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Acme Partnership's ordinary income is calculated as follows:

Sales | $200,000
COGS | (115,000)
Interest expense on bank line of credit | (13,000)
Administrative expenses | (50,000)
Ordinary income | $22,000
questions.explanationJa: 通常の所得には、パートナー段階で特別な扱いを受けない項目だけを含める。通常の所得は、売上$200,000−売上原価$115,000−銀行の与信枠に係る支払利息$13,000−管理費$50,000＝$22,000である。寄附金$2,000と長期キャピタルゲイン$10,000は個別記載項目なので含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.49

questions.stem: Which of the following is an accurate list of items that must be separately stated on Form 1065, U.S. Return of Partnership Income, Schedule K-1?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Section 1231 losses, investment interest, tax credits.

questions.explanation:
Partnerships must file an annual information return (Form 1065) and report ordinary business income, losses, and separately stated items. Form 1065 also includes the allocation of those amounts to each partner in a Schedule K-1. Partners then include their Schedule K-1 amounts in their own tax returns. The purpose of separately stating items is to allow for any special treatment on the partners' own tax returns.

Any item that would be included in the gross income of a partner, without restrictions or limitations (sales revenue), is included in the partnership's ordinary income or loss calculation.

("Charitable contributions, salaries, capital gains.") Charitable contributions and capital gains are separately stated. However, salaries are a deduction used in calculating partnership ordinary income.

("Sales revenue, dividends, depreciation.") Dividends are separately stated. However, sales revenue and depreciation are used in the calculation of partnership ordinary income.

("Wages, passive activities, rent.") Passive activities are separately stated. However, wages and rent are deductions used in calculating partnership ordinary income.
questions.explanationJa: 個別記載項目は、パートナーの申告で特別な扱いを受けるため、通常の事業所得と分けてSchedule K-1に記載する。Section 1231の損失、投資利息、税額控除はいずれもパートナー段階で制限や特別な計算があるので、すべて個別記載項目となる。他の組合せは、給与・売上・減価償却費・賃金・賃借料といった、通常の所得の計算に含める項目が混じっているため誤りである（寄附金・キャピタルゲイン・配当・パッシブ活動は個別記載）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.50

questions.stem: At partnership inception, Black acquires a 25% interest in Decorators Partnership by contributing property with an adjusted tax basis of $250,000. Black recognizes a gain if

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fair market value of the contributed property exceeds its adjusted tax basis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The property is encumbered by a mortgage with a balance of $100,000 that is assumed by the partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The adjusted tax basis of the contributed property exceeds its fair market value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The net liability relief due to the partnership assuming a mortgage exceeds the property's adjusted tax basis.

questions.explanation:
For example, if Black's property in this scenario were subject to a $340,000 mortgage, the net liability relief would be $255,000 ($340,000 − $85,000), which exceeds the property's $250,000 adjusted tax basis. Because Black's basis cannot be negative, it is adjusted to $0, and Black recognizes a $5,000 capital gain, as shown below.

Black's basis for contributed property: $250,000
Less: mortgage assumed by P/S: (340,000)
Plus: Black's share of P/S mortgage (25% × $340,000): 85,000
Basis before adjustment: ($5,000)
Capital gain recognized: 5,000
Black's basis in P/S: $0
questions.explanationJa: 財産の拠出は原則として非課税だが、パートナーシップが負債を引き受けたことによる正味の負債免除額が、拠出財産の帳簿価額を超えるとベーシスがマイナスになるため、その超過額を利得として認識する。たとえば$340,000の抵当債務が付いていれば、正味の負債免除は$340,000−25%持分の$85,000＝$255,000となり、帳簿価額$250,000を$5,000上回る。ベーシスはマイナスにならないので$0に調整され、$5,000のキャピタルゲインを認識する。時価と帳簿価額の差があるだけでは利得は生じない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.51

questions.stem:
George and Martha are equal partners in G&M Partnership. At the beginning of the current tax year, the adjusted basis of George's partnership interest was $32,500, which included his 50% share of $40,000 of partnership liabilities. During the tax year, the following information applied to G&M:

Ordinary business loss | ($30,000)
Interest and dividend income | 8,000
Partnership liabilities at end of the year | 24,000

What was the basis of George's partnership interest at end of the current year?
questions.explanation:
George's $32,500 beginning basis is decreased by 50% of the P/S ordinary business loss and increased by 50% of the interest and dividend income. Half of the $16,000 ($40,000 − $24,000) reduction in P/S liabilities decreases the basis. Accordingly, George's ending basis is $13,500.

Beginning basis: $32,500
Less share of P/S loss ($30,000 × 50%): (15,000)
Plus share of interest and dividends ($8,000 × 50%): 4,000
Less share of decrease in P/S liabilities ($16,000 × 50%): (8,000)
Ending basis: $13,500
questions.explanationJa: Georgeの期首ベーシス$32,500から、通常事業損失の持分$30,000×50%＝$15,000を引き、受取利息・配当の持分$8,000×50%＝$4,000を加える。パートナーシップ負債は$40,000から$24,000へ$16,000減少したので、その50%の$8,000もベーシスを減らす。よって期末ベーシスは$32,500−$15,000＋$4,000−$8,000＝$13,500である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.52

questions.stem: What is the tax treatment of net losses in excess of the at-risk amount for an activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any loss in excess of the at-risk amount is suspended and is deductible in the year in which the activity is disposed of in full.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any losses in excess of the at-risk amount are suspended and carried forward without expiration and are deductible against income in future years from that activity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any losses in excess of the at-risk amount are deducted currently against income from other activities; the remaining loss, if any, is carried forward without expiration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any losses in excess of the at-risk amount are carried back two years against activities with income and then carried forward for 20 years.

questions.explanation:
Loss deductions incurred in the production of income or in a trade or business are limited to the taxpayer's at-risk amount in that activity. For partnerships (P/S), when a business loss is incurred a partner's share of the P/S's ordinary business loss is deductible to the extent of basis, at-risk, and passive activity limitations.

Losses may not reduce the partner's basis in the P/S below zero.

Losses are further limited by the partner's at-risk amount in the P/S. Because some partners may not be liable for P/S debt, the at-risk rules prevent partners from deducting losses greater than their personal liabilities in the P/S. The amount at risk equals a partner's basis less any nonrecourse debt (not personally liable), such as a loan that uses P/S inventory as collateral.

If the P/S activity is passive, losses are further limited to the partner's passive income, not active and portfolio income.

Any losses suspended (not currently deductible) based on these limitations are carried forward indefinitely to future years until the partner has sufficient basis, at-risk amounts, or passive income.
questions.explanationJa: パートナーが控除できるパートナーシップの事業損失は、ベーシス、アットリスク額、パッシブ活動の各制限の範囲内に限られる。アットリスク額は、ベーシスからパートナーが個人的に責任を負わないノンリコース債務を除いた額である。これらの制限で当期に控除できなかった損失は、期限なく将来に繰り越され、その活動から十分なアットリスク額や所得が生じた年に控除できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.53

questions.stem:
On June 1, Year 1, two individuals formed a partnership as equal partners by contributing the assets below:

Asset | Adjusted tax basis | Fair market value
Partner A | Cash | $100,000 | $100,000
Partner B | Equipment | 60,000 | 80,000

The partnership incurred $10,000 of recourse debt and $18,000 of nonrecourse debt on June 2, Year 1. Operations began on June 3, Year 1. What was Partner B's tax basis and at-risk basis in the partnership interest on June 2, Year 1?
Tax basis | At-risk basis
questions.explanation:
At-risk rules prevent partners from deducting losses greater than the amount of their personal liability. Because partners do not bear the risk of loss for nonrecourse liabilities (secured by collateral), these liabilities do not generally provide basis for deducting losses. Therefore, the at-risk basis excludes P/S nonrecourse debt.

Although Partner B's tax basis is $74,000, the at-risk basis is only $65,000; nonrecourse debt accounts for the difference.

Equipment contributed (adjusted tax basis) | $60,000
Share of recourse debt (50% × $10,000) | 5,000
Share of nonrecourse debt (50% × $18,000) | 9,000
Partner B's tax basis | $74,000
Less: nonrecourse debt | (9,000)
Partner B's at-risk basis | $65,000
questions.explanationJa: 財産を拠出した場合のベーシスは調整後の税務上の帳簿価額で計算し、パートナーシップ負債の持分相当額を加える。ノンリコース債務は損失リスクを負わないので、アットリスク額からは除く。Partner Bの税務ベーシスは、設備$60,000＋リコース債務50%×$10,000＝$5,000＋ノンリコース債務50%×$18,000＝$9,000＝$74,000である。ノンリコース分$9,000を除いたアットリスク・ベーシスは$65,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.54

questions.stem: On January 2, Year 4, Black acquired a 50% interest in Newt Partnership by contributing property with an adjusted basis of $7,000 and a fair market value of $25,000, subject to a mortgage of $18,000 that was assumed by the partnership. What amount of gain or loss, if any, will Black report as a result of the contribution?
questions.explanation:
Black contributed property with an adjusted basis of $7,000, subject to an $18,000 mortgage assumed by the P/S. Because Black's basis in the P/S cannot be negative, the basis is adjusted up to $0 and a $2,000 gain is recognized as shown below:

Basis of contributed property | $7,000
Less: mortgage assumed by P/S | (18,000)
Plus: Black's 50% share P/S mortgage | 9,000
Basis before adjustment for gain | ($2,000)
Capital gain recognized | 2,000
Basis | $0
questions.explanationJa: Blackが拠出した財産の帳簿価額は$7,000で、パートナーシップが$18,000の抵当債務を引き受け、Blackはその50%の$9,000を負担する。ベーシスは$7,000−$18,000＋$9,000＝−$2,000となるが、マイナスにはできないので$0に調整し、$2,000の利得を認識する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.55

questions.stem: Kline and Salomon form the KS Partnership as 50/50 partners. Salomon contributes cash of $45,000. Kline contributes equipment that has a fair market value of $60,000 and an adjusted basis of $45,000. In addition, the equipment is subject to a $10,000 loan that KS Partnership is assuming. What amount represents Salomon's initial basis in the partnership?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Salomon's basis (before adjustment) equals the $45,000 cash contributed. However, because Kline (the other partner) contributed equipment subject to a $10,000 loan assumed by the P/S, Salomon is liable for $5,000 ($10,000 × 50%), which is half of the debt. Accordingly, Salomon's basis is increased by $5,000, resulting in an initial basis of $50,000 ($45,000 + $5,000).
questions.explanationJa: Salomonの調整前のベーシスは、拠出した現金$45,000である。Klineが持ち込んだ設備の借入$10,000をパートナーシップが引き受けたので、Salomonはその50%の$5,000を負担し、ベーシスに加える。よってSalomonの当初ベーシスは$45,000＋$5,000＝$50,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.56

questions.stem: Johnson, an individual, has a 50% interest in DEF Partnership. Johnson's adjusted basis at the beginning of the year was $14,000. The partnership's ordinary income for the current year was $6,000. Johnson received a nonliquidating distribution of $8,000 cash, and property with an adjusted basis of $12,000 and a fair market value of $15,000. What is the basis of the distributed property, other than cash, to Johnson?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, current ordinary income increases Johnson's partnership basis by $3,000 (50% interest × $6,000) to $17,000 ($14,000 beginning basis + $3,000 income). Johnson's basis is then reduced by the $8,000 cash distribution ($9,000 remaining basis = $17,000 basis − $8,000 cash). Johnson's basis is further reduced by the property's carryover basis ($12,000) but is limited to Johnson's $9,000 remaining basis. Therefore, Johnson's basis in the property is $9,000.
questions.explanationJa: 当期の通常所得の持分50%×$6,000＝$3,000でベーシスは$14,000＋$3,000＝$17,000に増え、そこから現金の分配$8,000を引いて$9,000が残る。資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額$12,000は残りのベーシス$9,000に制限されるので、分配された資産のベーシスは$9,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.57

questions.stem:
Brooke and Bulstrode are equal partners in the B&B Partnership, a cash basis tax entity with the following balance sheet items:

Adjusted tax basis | Fair market value
Cash | $250 | $250
Accounts receivable | 0 | 300
Total assets | $250 | $550
Accounts payable | $150 | $150
Brooke, capital | 50 | 200
Bulstrode, capital | 50 | 200
Total liabilities and capital | $250 | $550

On the balance sheet date, Brooke purchases Bulstrode's 50% interest in the partnership, paying Bulstrode $300 cash and assuming Bulstrode's share of the partnership liabilities. As a result of this buyout of her partnership interest, what is the capital gain on sale that Bulstrode should report on her individual tax return?
questions.explanation:
Generally, the sale of a P/S interest is a capital gain (loss) because it results from the sale of a capital asset. At the time of sale, if the P/S has unrealized ordinary income assets, referred to as hot assets (unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory), the partner has effectively converted ordinary income to capital gains. To prevent this, the capital gain is recharacterized as ordinary income to the extent of the partner's share of hot assets at the time of sale.

In this scenario, Bulstrode realized a gain of $250, as calculated below. Because the P/S has a hot asset (unrealized accounts receivable [A/R]), $150 of the gain is recharacterized as ordinary. Accordingly, Bulstrode reports a capital gain of $100 ($250 − $150).

Cash received: $300
Relief of liabilities ($150 × 50%): 75
Amount realized: $375
Less adjusted outside basis ($50 capital + $75 liabilities): (125)
Realized gain: $250
Recharacterized as ordinary income ($300 A/R × 50%): (150)
Reported as capital gain: $100
questions.explanationJa: 持分の売却は原則として資本資産の売却でありキャピタルゲインとなるが、パートナーシップにホットアセット（未実現債権や含み益のある棚卸資産）がある場合、その持分相当額は通常所得として扱う。Bulstrodeの実現額は、現金$300＋負債の免除$150×50%＝$75で$375である。外部ベーシスは資本$50＋負債$75＝$125なので、実現利得は$375−$125＝$250となる。現金主義の売掛金$300の50%＝$150を通常所得とするため、キャピタルゲインは$250−$150＝$100である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.58
